texts.facts: Judgment: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of t he PFA Act and Rules. 2. As per the complaint, on 08.08.2002, the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) Sh D.P. Singh and FI N.N. Sharma under the supervision of Local Health Authority (herein after referred to DA vs Chander Kumar etc as LHA)/SDM Sh G.R. Meena visited the premises of M/s Shyamlal & Brothers, Shop No. 1752, Nai Basti, S.P. Mukherjee Marg, Delhi, where the accused Chander Kumar was found conducting the business in the above mention shop, having stored various food articles including "Kuber Readymade Scented Khaini" for sale for human consumption. The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of "Kuber Readymade Scented Khaini" from the vendor for analysis. The sample consisted 6 X 250 gms sealed polythene packets of "Kuber Readymade scented Khaini" taken as such bearing label declaration as mentioned in form-VI. The sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh. G.R. Meena, SDM/LHA. The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three parts. Each counter part containing the sample was separately packed fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample counter parts. Notice was given to accused No. 1 Chander Kumar and the price of sample was also given to him vide vendor receipt dated 8-8-2002. Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by F.I. were signed by accused No. 1 Chander Kumar and the other witness Sh. N.N. Shanna, FI. Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such Sh. N.N. Shanna, FI was joined as witness. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA code No. GRM/LHA/002145 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and two counter-pans were deposited with the LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found DA vs Chander Kumar etc the Khaini to be conforming to the standards but sweetened supari is adulterated. The report of the Public Analyst is as follows: "The sample of scented khaini is not adulterated but sweetened supari is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz. Tartrazine use of colour is not allowed in supari. Supari pouch is also misbranded as the declaration for colour & artificial sweeterner are not made as per the requirement of Rule-24 and Rule-42 ZZZ(1). 4. At the time of analysing the sample Public Analyst found that "Kuber Ready made scented khaini sample in original sealed small pouches of 10 grns. each, 25 such pouches are contained in another original polythene packet with declaration of one free pouch whose details are not given on this packet complies with Rule-32" and alter analysis opined vide report number PFA/Enf.1277/2002 dated 3-9-2002 that the sample of scented khaini is not adulterated but sweetened supari is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz. Tartrazine use of colour is not allowed in supari. 5. It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Chander Kumar was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Shyam Lal & Brothers, Shop No.1752. Nai Basti. S.P. Muhherjee Marg, Delhi-6 at the time of sampling and is in charge of and responsible for the day to day conduct of the business of the said shop. The sampled DA vs Chander Kumar etc food article has been purchased by the vendor from M/s New Delhi Marketing Co., A-145, Ganesh Nagar, New Delhi-18 which is a proprietorship concern and accused No. 2 Smt. Suman Khatter is the proprietor of the concern and as such she is in charge of and responsible for the day to day conduct of the said business. Accused No.2 Smt. Suman Khatter has disclosed that the sampled food article was purchased from accused No.3 M/s Kuber Khaini Private Private Ltd, 32, K, Siraspur, GT Kamal Road, Delhi-42. Accused No. 3 M/s Kuber Khaini Private Ltd. had appointed accused No. 4 Hari Rain Production Manager as its nominee under the PFA Act at the time of sampling & as such the nominee accused No. 4 Hari Ram and the company are liable and responsible for the day to day conduct of the said business. 6. It is further stated that accused No. 3 M/s Kuber Khaini Pvt. Ltd. disclosed that free pouches of Supari which were packed along with the "Kuber ready made scented Khaini" were purchased from accused No.5 M/s Kuber Grains & Spices Pvt. Ltd. Khasra No. 1282, Kapashera Village, New Delhi-110037. Accused No.5 M/s Kuber Grains & Spieces P Ltd. is having two directors namely accused No.6 Raj Kumar Malu and accused No.7 Lakshmi Pati Jain. As there was no nominee appointed by the company at the time of sampling both the directors are responsible along with the company for the day to day conduct of the said business. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 03.11.2003 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(j)(m) and section 2(ix)(k) of PFA Rules, DA vs Chander Kumar etc 1955 as well as Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 and Rule 24 & 42 ZZZ(1) of PFA Rules 1955 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused. 8. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 07.11.2001. Based on the report of the PA charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(j)(m), Section 2(ix(k) of PFA Act 1954 and Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 of PFA Rules, Rule 24 and 42 (ZZZ)(1) of PFA Rule 1955, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 9. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI Arun Kumar, PW-2 FI N.N. Sharma and PW- 3 SDM/LHA Sh G.R. Meena. PW-2 and FI Sh D.P. Singh were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh G.R.Meena. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of six original sealed polythene packets of 250 gms each of "Kuber Readymade Scented Khaini", bearing identical label declaration from the accused, dividing the sample commodity into three equal parts by putting 2 sealed packets together as one counterpart, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-2/A, DA vs Chander Kumar etc Notice in Form-VI Ex.PW-2/B and Panchnama Ex.PW-1/D. The vendor disclosed the source of purchase of sample commodity on the spot and handed over purchase bill Mark X-14. A notice u/s 14-A Ex.PW2/C was also prepared at the spot addressed to supplier M/s New Delhi Marketing Company. Thereafter two counterpart of the sample commodity were deposited on the next working day, under intimation that one counterpart of the same has already been deposited with PA. Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW3/A was received which revealed that the sample was not adulterated but of sweetned supari was adulterated and was also misbranded. Thereafter the matter was marked to PW-1 FI Arun Kumar, who on the direction of SDM/LHA started the investigation and sent letter Ex.PW1/A to vendor and received its reply Ex.PW1/A-1 alongwith document Mark-X and X-1. Thereafter PW-1 FI Arun Kumar sent letter Ex.PW1/B and reminder Ex.PW1/B-1 to New Delhi Marketing company and received its reply Ex.PW1/B-2 alongwith photocopy of bill Mrk X-2. PW-1 FI Arun Kumar also sent letter Ex.PW1/C to Kuber Khaini P Ltd and received reply Ex.PW1/C-1. PW-1 FI Arun Kumar again sent letter Ex.PW1/C-2 and reminder Ex.PW1/C-3 to Kuber Khani P Ltd and received reply Ex.PW1/C-4 alongwith photocopy of nomination in Form VIII Mark X-3. PW-1 FI Arun Kumar also sent letter ExPW1/D to Kuber and received reply Ex.PW1/D-1 alongwith photocopy of nomination in form-VII Mark X-4 and minutes of meeting mark X-5 and photocopy of invoice Mark X-6 to 10. Thereafter PW-1 FI Arun Kumar verified from PFA office regarding nominee of M/s Kuber Khaini P Ltd vide letter Ex.PW1/E and received reply and document Mark X-11 and X-12 from LHA. Thereafter on completion of investigation, the entire DA vs Chander Kumar etc case file was sent to concern SDM/LHA who forwarded the then Director, PFA Sh. S.N. Bansal for obtaining his consent for Da vs Chander Kumar Etc on 16 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64226644/ 4 prosecution of accused persons and the then Director, PFA after applying his mind granted his consent for prosecution Ex.PW1/F. Thereafter, the present complaint Ex.PW1/G was filed before the Court and then intimation letter Ex. PW1/H along with copy of PA Report were sent to the accused persons through registered post mark X-13. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel. 10. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 10.08.2016 wherein the accused persons denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Thereafter the matter was listed for defence evidence. The accused chose not to lead DE and vide order dated 08.11.2016 the defence evidence was closed and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
texts.arguments: In The State of Punjab v. National Organic Chemical Industries Ltd., JT (1996) 10 SC 480 this Court in somewhat similar circumstances said that the procedure laid down under Section 24 of the Act deprived the accused to have sample tested by the Central Insecticides Laboratory and adduce evidence of the report so given in his defence. In this connection reference be made to decisions of this Court in State of Haryana v. Brij Lal Mittal & Ors., [1998] 5 SCC 343 under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940; Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Ghisa Ram, AIR (1967) SC 970; Chetumal v. State of Madhya Pradesh & Anr., DA vs Chander Kumar etc [1981] 3 SCC 72 and Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf & Anr., [1999] 2 SCC 400 all under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. Therefore, placing reliance upon the aforesaid judgement of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Da vs Chander Kumar Etc on 16 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64226644/ 6 State of Haryana vs Unique Farmaid P. Ltd & Ors, Hindustan Liver Ltd Vs State of Punjab 2011 (1) FAC 192, a benefit of doubt is given to the accused regarding the adulteration of the sample, which is the subject matter of the present case. Reliance may further be had upon the case titled as Food Inspector vs Banarsi Das & Ors 2014 (2) FAC 177 wherein the order of declining cognizance was uphold by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi when the complaint was filed after expiry period of the product more particularly when no preservative was added to the sample as per the prosecution evidence. Reliance may further be had on the judgement of Marico Ltd and others vs State of Delhi 2015 (1) FAC 40. 16.Regarding misbranding The judgment of Gokul Krishnan (supra) has also been followed in the judgment of M/s Bunge India Pvt Ltd & Others vs State & Another Crl.MC 439/2008 dated 20.01.2011. 17.
